author: WP02
summary: The unit classifies how dependencies are acquired (submodules, in-tree sources, siblings, fetches, host packages), the configure-time SDL build, host-package gates, the sibling contract, renderer dependency asymmetry, build-tree consumption and the C package, then the CnaTests corpus, examples, presets and the authority classes of developer tools. At TARGET the submodule set, the FFmpeg omission model, the preset set and the sanitizer presets changed and there is no in-tree wgpu-native area. The Development pages had pins and overrides; the reproducibility reasoning, composition, failure states, sibling details and the evidence classes went into two new deep dives.

concepts.section: Dependencies, Tests, Examples, and Developer Tools
concepts.text: A configure can involve submodules, sibling repositories, system packages, downloaded sources, prebuilt binaries and SDKs; calling them all 'vendored' hides the most common reproducibility failures.

concepts.section: Five acquisition mechanisms
concepts.text: Git submodules at TARGET are five gitlinks: SDL, SDL_image, SDL_mixer, draco and vendor/googletest; an archive may omit them.

concepts.section: Five acquisition mechanisms
concepts.text: In-tree sources are cgltf, stb, ENet and dr_libs; there is no in-tree wgpu-native area (the native WebGPU renderer downloads an official release, the browser build uses Emscripten's port).

concepts.section: The unusual SDL configure-time build
concepts.text: With the default vendored route CMake configures, builds and installs SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer during CNA's configure into a persistent prefix outside the build directory and consumes their exported packages; CNA_USE_SYSTEM_SDL switches to find_package.

concepts.section: The unusual SDL configure-time build
concepts.text: Deleting or cleaning a CNA build directory does not rebuild SDL; at TARGET the install is reused only while its build manifest matches.
tokens: Deleting or cleaning a CNA build directory does not rebuild SDL

concepts.section: The unusual SDL configure-time build
concepts.text: The prefix is keyed by target system and processor so a cross-build does not overwrite a native installation (with Wayland, simulator and deployment-target suffixes at TARGET).

concepts.section: The unusual SDL configure-time build
concepts.text: A configure failure may be a nested dependency compile or install failure ('CNA: SDL3 cmake configure failed (exit code N)', 'build failed', 'install failed'), not a CNA CMake-language error.

concepts.section: The unusual SDL configure-time build
concepts.text: The default parallelism of the SDL sub-builds is intentionally small (CNA_MAX_VENDORED_BUILD_JOBS=2) because a parent -j does not limit separate CMake invocations.
